import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 15

References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.15)
- [BJP14] T. Brown, V. Jungić and A. Poelstra, "On double 3-term arithmetic progressions",
  Integers 14 (2014), Paper No. A43.
- [CCS14] J. Cassaigne, J. D. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, "Avoidance of additive cubes and
  related results", Adv. in Appl. Math. 56 (2014), 25–66.
-/

open Set
open scoped NNReal

namespace Green15

/--
Does there exist a Lipschitz function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose graph
$\Gamma = \{(n, f(n)) : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2$ is free of 3-term progressions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_15 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 3 := by
  sorry

/--
The answer is YES for 4-term progressions [BJP14].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_15_ap4 :
    ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree  {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 4 := by
  sorry

-- TODO(jeangud) Add finitary version

end Green15

findings.description: The module bibliography’s [CCS14] entry (lines 26–27) gives the wrong title and publication details: “Avoidance of additive cubes and related results”, Adv. in Appl. Math. 56 (2014), 25–66. The relevant paper is “Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum”, published in J. ACM. This is a bibliographic error only; both Lean statements are mathematically faithful.
findings.source_evidence: Green’s cited problem list, reference [65], identifies J. Cassaigne, J. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, “Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum”, J. ACM 61 (2014), no. 2, Art. 10, 17 pp. Shallit’s 2014 publication list confirms these details, and arXiv:1106.5204 contains the paper and its additive-cube avoidance result. Sources: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf and https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~shallit/papers.html.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace [CCS14] with: J. Cassaigne, J. D. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, “Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum”, J. ACM 61 (2014), no. 2, Article 10, 17 pp. Optionally link https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.5204.

reformulations.difference: BJP14, page 3, gives an increasing sequence of positive integers with bounded gaps and no double 4-term arithmetic progression. Lean allows an arbitrary integer-valued Lipschitz function and requires its graph to contain no nontrivial 4-term progression.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given a Lean witness f with Lipschitz constant K, choose an integer M > K and set g(n) = f(n) + M*n + 1 - f(0). Then g(0) = 1 and 0 < g(n+1)-g(n) ≤ M+K, so g is positive, strictly increasing, and has bounded gaps. The invertible affine map (x,y) ↦ (x,y+M*x+1-f(0)) preserves and reflects nontrivial arithmetic progressions and sends the graph of f to that of g. Conversely, an increasing bounded-gap sequence is Lipschitz by telescoping. A double 4-term progression is exactly a 4-term progression in its graph; shifting indexing between 0 and 1 is harmless. Thus these existence statements are equivalent.

sources_consulted: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.15 — currently served December 2025 revision; Problem 15, its comments, and references [58] and [65].
https://math.colgate.edu/~integers/o43/o43.pdf — Brown–Jungić–Poelstra, especially the introduction, the 4-term result on page 3, and the bounded-gap equivalences in Section 4.
https://arxiv.org/e-print/1106.5204 — Cassaigne–Currie–Schaeffer–Shallit, LaTeX source; introduction, construction, additive-cube theorem, two-sided variant, and open problems.
review.notes: Both declarations match Green’s Problem 15 and its 4-term remark. Green’s current source still records the 3-term question as open and the 4-term variant as established; BJP14 page 3 is a valid secondary citation for the latter. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and more_checks.lean compiled successfully: they confirm the usual absolute-value metrics, an infinite graph, the intended nontrivial-AP semantics, and exclusion of K=0 for both lengths. A finite prefix of the cited additive-cube construction also passed computational checks. The source’s graph display has an apparent n∈ℤ typo despite specifying f:ℕ→ℤ; Lean follows the specified domain and the one-sided constructions. The supplementary erdosproblems.com/193 link was blocked by Cloudflare, but the cited sources sufficed to verify both declarations.
